Child and Youth Behavioral School Military and Family Life Counselor (CYBS-MFLC)
Contingent Upon Contract Award and successful completion of program required background check.

The Child and Youth Behavioral School Military and Family Life Counselor (CYBS-MFLC) provides non-medical counseling, consultation, prevention, education, and outreach services to military-connected students in Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) schools and Local Education Agency (LEA) schools that serve military families. The CYBS-MFLC supports student well-being, resilience, academic success, and family readiness by helping children and adolescents navigate the unique challenges associated with military life.

The CYBS-MFLC delivers services through a visible, embedded, relationship-based model within school communities, engaging students, educators, caregivers, and military support partners in natural educational settings to promote resilience, early intervention, and successful adjustment

Using a short-term, solution-focused, strengths-based approach, the CYBS-MFLC assists students in developing effective coping skills, improving social-emotional functioning, building resilience, and successfully managing military-related transitions. Services are preventive in nature and delivered in accordance with Department of War (DoW) Military and Family Life Counseling Program requirements.

Through prevention, early intervention, consultation, and resilience-building services, the CYBS-MFLC strengthens student well-being, supports academic success, and contributes to overall military family readiness and mission effectiveness
